item.title: 🎙 Russian Ambassador to Seychelles Kirill Sokolov-Shcherbachev’s comment regarding Russia-Seychelles cooperation in the field of tourism
item.description: 🎙 Russian Ambassador to Seychelles Kirill Sokolov-Shcherbachev’s comment regarding Russia-Seychelles cooperation in the field of tourism (4 September 2026) #Tourism 💬 Tourism is the leading area of our cooperation with Seychelles and it is now on the rise. For Seychelles tourism is the main source of income. The tourist industry suffered a lot when the air connectivity with Gulf countries was broken because of the Middle East crisis. Even after it has been partially restored, that is Russia which kept providing Seychelles with the tourist flow . Aeroflot flights have never stopped, although the flight time has increased. #Aeroflot Moreover, this year it has been decided to make Aeroflot flight all year-round , instead of seasonal timetable (September-May). 🎙
Russian Ambassador to Seychelles Kirill Sokolov-Shcherbachev’s
comment
regarding Russia-Seychelles cooperation in the field of tourism
(4 September 2026)
#Tourism
💬
Tourism is the leading area of our cooperation with Seychelles
and it is now on the rise. For Seychelles tourism is the main source of income. The tourist industry suffered a lot when the air connectivity with Gulf countries was broken because of the Middle East crisis. Even after it has been partially restored,
that is Russia which kept providing Seychelles with the tourist flow
. Aeroflot flights have never stopped, although the flight time has increased.
#Aeroflot
Moreover, this year it has been decided to make
Aeroflot
flight
all year-round
, instead of seasonal timetable (September-May). After a short period,
flights have resumed on 8 July
. Currently, Aeroflot is operating
twice a week
and it is fully booked. In the winter period they add one more flight. 2025 counts
more than 43,000 passengers
, most of which are tourists. Guests from Russia make
15%
of the whole tourist flow
. Our country is on the third place after Germany and France. We will see what are the figures by the end of this year because, according to local estimates, sometimes
our tourists are ahead
.
#Russianlanguage
There are Russian-speaking tourist operators in Seychelles.
And the use of Russian language in the field of tourism is increasing.
We see Russian-speaking personnel in hotels and travel agencies, tour guides, advertisement etc. The Seychelles Tourism Academy (STA) is providing Russian language courses for more than
100 students
studying in different areas of tourist industry. It doesn’t mean that all of them will fluently speak Russian in a couple of months, but I am sure that
this is just the beginning
and it may be useful for some of them in their future professional activity.
Recently, we agreed the management of
Savoy
and
Coral Strand hotels
, which host a large number of Russians, and the STA to launch
a project for students
to help the reception desk in welcoming Russian guests and practicing their Russian language skills. Of course, we do not expect them to literally “sing” in Russian, they are just beginners. But anyway, I think this initiative is working for the nice image of the hotel and help the young specialists to overpass the language barrier. So, the Russian tourists, in particular those, who come to Seychelles in group by Aeroflot, can be warmly welcomed by Seychellois students at the hotel.
🤝
We count on keeping up the good figures in Russian arrivals and maybe even on their rise. At the same time we will continue to work on
further improving the tourist services
, for example, in expanding the Russian language in this field.
🇷🇺
🇸🇨
#RussiaSeychelles

▪️
On September 8, 1941, the
Siege of Leningrad began
— one of the most horrific and tragic events not only of the Great Patriotic War but of the entire World War II.
The siege lasted for 872 days and claimed the lives of approximately 1 million residents of the city, including more than
600'000 people
who died from starvation.
Alongside German troops, military units from European countries conquered by Hitler participated in the Siege of Leningrad —
the 'Norway', 'the Netherlands' and 'Flanders' legions,
as well as the Spanish infantry division. From the Narva direction, Baltic units —
Latvian and Estonian battalions
— were kept in reserve by the Nazis. From the north, the
Finnish army
besieged Leningrad and also shelled the city with its artillery.
The Nazis and their accomplices
planned to wipe Leningrad off the face of the Earth
and subject its population to
complete annihilation,
including by creating conditions for mass starvation, destroying food supplies, and cutting off supply routes.
***
In early September 1941, during the Leningrad Defensive Operation of the Red Army, the city was cut off by the Nazis from all land routes. On September 8, Hitler's troops captured Shlisselburg, completing the encirclement. The city was bombarded daily with artillery.
The Nazi command's orders were absolutely clear:
maintain the siege,
strictly enforce the blockade, shoot anyone crossing the front line, and bring about the total destruction of the city's population.
❗️
But Leningrad endured and never stopped fighting.
Under unbearable conditions, the city's industrial enterprises continued to operate. During the blockade, workers produced or repaired about
2'000 tanks, 1'500 aircraft, 850 warships and vessels
of various classes, as well as
225'000 submachine guns,
12'000 mortars, and 7.5 million shells and mines.
The most famous memorial to the victims of the blockade is the Piskaryovskoye Memorial Cemetery in Saint Petersburg — the largest mass military grave of World War II. Over
420'000 Leningrad residents and 70'000 defenders
of the city are buried there.
#Victory81
🌟
The blockade was finally lifted on
January 27, 1944,
during the Leningrad–Novgorod Offensive.
***
In 2022, at the request of the Prosecutor General’s Office of Russia, the Saint Petersburg City Court officially recognised the actions of the German occupying forces — along with their collaborators, including armed units formed in Belgium, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands, Norway, and Finland, as well as individual volunteers from Austria, Latvia, Poland, France, and Czechoslovakia —
as a war crime, a crime against humanity, and an act of
genocide
against national and ethnic groups representing the population of the Soviet Union.

🎙
Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman
Maria Zakharova
’s
answer to a media question
regarding the new EU human rights report
(September 7, 2026)
❓
Question: In August, the EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy released its annual report on human rights and democracy around the world for 2025. What is your assessment of this document?
💬
Maria Zakharova:
Yes, we have seen it. And frankly,
it is a perfect compilation of all the EU’s favourite clichés and slogans:
the usual self-promotion of their supposed role as a “global champion of human rights,” a laundry list of politicised accusations against third countries, alongside intrusive and patronising lecturing.
What’s more, the level of criticism isn’t calibrated to the facts on the ground but is determined solely by how pliant each state is towards Brussels.
A case in point: the section on Ukraine, which is utterly toothless and, in places, almost fawning – this for
a country mired in corruption, lawlessness, and neo-Nazi ideology.
It is telling that
Brussels no longer even bothers to hide its use of the human rights agenda as a cover for blatant interference in the internal affairs
of states that pursue independent policies. They openly admit to funnelling significant funds into “civil society,” media, journalists, and activists in targeted countries with the explicit aim of shaping domestic politics and steering foreign policy choices.
One passage in particular stands out: how the EU frames its own policy towards Russia. In the country-specific section, they unabashedly call it a
“wartime approach”
–
as if that somehow justifies their glaring lies about our country,
their double standards, and their willingness to sweep under the rug the EU’s own violations of our citizens’ rights.
❗️
In essence,
Brussels is openly declaring that it intends to weaponise human rights as leverage against Russia.
Throughout the report, Brussels once again presumes to speak from a self-appointed moral high ground, casting itself as a “force for good in the world.” These statements look particularly cynical against the backdrop of the EU’s own
steadily deteriorating human rights record.
Intolerance is on the rise across the bloc, with racism and hate speech becoming increasingly frequent. European institutions either turn a blind eye to Russophobia, including its most grotesque manifestations – or, worse, actively condone it.
The shameful reality of mass statelessness in the Baltics
, alongside the systematic denial of education in their native language to local Russian-speaking populations, is a glaring case in point.
For all their outward talk of democracy and the rule of law, inside the EU they are clamping down on dissent through censorship, bans on inconvenient media outlets, and the silencing of political actors who dare to criticise current Brussels policies.
All of this is dressed up as “safeguarding democracy” when, in fact, what they are doing is engineering a more pliable socio-political environment, tightening their grip on the information space and on the will of their own citizens.
For a more accurate picture of the real human rights situation in Europe, including in Ukraine, I would refer you to
the joint report published in June by the Russian and Belarusian Foreign Ministries, entitled “Human Rights Situation in Certain Countries.”
It is available in English, so that anyone interested, including international audiences, can judge for themselves which document shows genuine concern for human rights.
☝️
And I think we can safely say that
the comparison will not reflect well on the opus signed by Kaja Kallas.

🎙
Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's
response
to a question from
RBC
(RosBusinessConsulting)
on the US deployment of a launcher for intermediate- and shorter-range missiles in Norway
(September 7, 2026)
❓
Question: How does Moscow assess the US deployment of a launcher for intermediate- and shorter-range missiles in Norway, including in the context of the stalled strategic stability dialogue? Is any response planned? If so, what kind?
💬
Maria Zakharova:
We regard the appearance in Europe of US systems capable of launching intermediate- and shorter-range missiles as
yet another step in the endless series of acutely destabilising actions by NATO countries.
In pursuing plans to deploy Western ground-launched intermediate- and shorter-range missiles in the region, NATO not only makes no secret of its intention but
openly flaunts its ambition to acquire a substantial capability to strike deep into Russia’s territory
.
At the same time,
NATO is seeking to bring vast maritime areas of the region within its sights
, establishing dominant control over sea routes of critical military, commercial and transport importance.
In this context, we note that the US missile systems equipped with
Mk 41 launching systems
, which are being brought into Europe and have now been deployed in Norway,
are capable of launching a wide range of missiles against both land and maritime targets
.
☝️
We also take into account that these systems can be used to launch
long-range Tomahawk cruise missiles
, while their deployment in Norway puts
a substantial part of Russia’s European territory, including Moscow, within range
.
Thus, these missile systems could be used in aggressive actions by NATO countries against our country to accomplish
strategic-level objectives
.
Those in Washington and Oslo who made the decision to deploy these systems in Norway should therefore not be surprised that, as part of Russia’s response measures, the deployment sites of the US systems, their command and control facilities, as well as the infrastructure supporting them,
are becoming a particular focus for Russia’s strategic deterrence forces
. This includes planning for the combat employment of the relevant strike assets in the event of an armed conflict.
***
As for the dialogue with the US on strategic stability, we would like to recall that it did not simply “stall”.
It was unilaterally suspended by the Joe Biden administration.
The current US authorities, meanwhile, are
unrealistically discussing the launch of some kind of “multilateral” negotiations with China’s mandatory participation
, even though Beijing has repeatedly and unequivocally stated that it has compelling reasons not to become involved in such work at this stage.
❗️
For our part, we have repeatedly explained in detail that
the conditions for a substantive and productive strategic dialogue with the US are not in place
.
Steps such as the deployment in Europe of US ground-launched intermediate- and shorter-range missiles that threaten Russia will, to put it mildly,
eliminate any basis for a constructive strategic dialogue with the US
.
